diagnosis_explanation: Your body has a problem called mesothelioma. This is a type of cancer. It affects the lining around your lungs. You also have a mass in the right side of your chest lining.
medication_rationale:
Albuterol Nebulizer Treatments:
This medicine helps you breathe easier.
It opens up your airways in your lungs.
You may feel your heart beat faster.
You might also feel shaky. These feelings often pass.
Call your doctor if you have chest pain.
Also call if your breathing gets worse.

Vicodin:
This medicine is for pain relief.
It helps to lessen your discomfort.
You may feel sleepy or dizzy.
You might also feel sick to your stomach.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
Also call if you feel very confused.
Important: Do not stop taking this medicine without calling your doctor first.
Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore after your procedure.
- Rest is important for healing.
- You can move around your home slowly.
- Do not lift, push, or pull anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Do not drive yourself anywhere.
- You can eat normally.
- Call your doctor if you have bad chest pain or trouble breathing.
- Your goal is to walk a little more each day.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a bit more energy.
- Soreness will likely get better.
- Continue to avoid lifting, pushing, or pulling over 10 pounds.
- You still cannot drive until your doctor says it is okay.
- Keep moving around your house gently.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F or chills.
- Your goal is to walk a bit further each day.

**Week 3:**
- You should notice less pain and more comfort.
- You can try doing light chores if you feel up to it.
- Keep following the lifting, pushing, and pulling limits.
- You can still not drive until cleared by your doctor.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
- Call your doctor if your surgical cut looks red or has fluid leaking.
- Your goal is to walk for 10 minutes without stopping.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel stronger and have more energy.
- You can likely do more everyday activities at home.
- Continue to not lift, push, or pull over 10 pounds.
- Ask your doctor about driving again.
- You can walk for longer periods.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening pain.
- Your goal is to walk outside for short periods.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Recovery takes time and varies for each person.
- Keep following the activity limits for now.
- Your doctor will tell you when it is safe to drive.
- Slowly increase your activity as you feel better.
- Attend all follow-up appointments.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- You cannot catch your breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Face drooping or arm weakness: These are stroke signs. Minutes matter.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: Pressure will not stop blood flow.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: You have become unresponsive.
- Seizure: Your body is having a major convulsion.
- Severe allergic reaction: Throat swelling or trouble breathing.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever above 101 degrees: You may have an infection.
- Severe pain medicine cannot help: Your pain is too bad.
- Wound looks infected: Red streaks or pus can spread.
- Cannot keep fluids down 12 hours: You need fluids right now.
- Confusion or new disorientation: Your thinking is getting worse.
- Fall with an injury: You may have broken bones.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly improving: Your pain is getting better.
- Questions about your Vicodin: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Questions about Albuterol: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Mild redness not spreading: Your wound is healing slowly.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen while you heal.
- Fatigue that is improving: You are starting to feel better.
